activity_context.topic_title: Changing the Order of Integration in Triple Integrals: Changing Region

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/63118a7b3d7fd589513f41ae1e721baf25305f480e683c984088fedb9a8d759b.png)

Change the order of integration in the integral

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x
$$

so that it is integrated first with respect to $x,$ then over a region $D$ in the $yz$-plane. The integration region $R$ is shown above.
feedback.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration ${u}_{1}(y,z)$ and ${u}_{2}(y,z)$ such that

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{u}_{1}(y,z)}^{{u}_{2}(y,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x]\text{d}A.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the region of integration $R$ can be written as a type III region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,\,:\,\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le z\le 2,\,\,0\le y\le \sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}x\,\text{d}A,$ we write $R$ as a type II region.

To visualize this, imagine firing an arrow through the region parallel to the $x$-axis and in the direction of increasing $x,$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/7dbabd349afb41c00c447ab61e28139cc7818a74c54bd17a61eb77d05ae558ae.png)

The arrow enters the region through the back boundary and leaves through the front boundary:

- The front boundary of the region, written in the form $x=x(y,z),$ is

$$
y=\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}\,⟹\,x=\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}.
$$

- The back boundary of the region is $x=0.$

Therefore, the type II representation of $R$ is

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,\,:\,\,(y,z)\in D,\,\,0\le x\le \sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14073682/assets/4040e2d2eadc5c39b9224b1b39980de486fe6dd69dad1e63179c6cffcb4046b4.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration so that it is integrated first with respect to $x$ and then over $D,$ we obtain

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x]\text{d}A.
$$
